correctness.rationale: For every N>=2 and positive friction, coupling and diffusivity, the stationary Gaussian is proven from the drift Lyapunov identity. Tilted generator, orthogonal skew mode splitting and Riccati Feynman–Kac solution establish the finite-N SCGF in an admissible interval containing the size-independent critical tilt; exact sine identity gives the cotangent free energy. Subtraction of harmonic singularity from the cosecant sum and smooth Riemann-sum error control yield the sharp derivative with O(1) remainder. An independent numerical checker passed 366 exact-identity, spectral and finite-time comparisons; numerical trials are corroboration, not infinity proofs.

originality.rationale: The general finite-dimensional OU entropy-production SCGF is acknowledged as covered by du Buisson–Touchette and Mazzolo–Monthus. The primary novel scientific assertion is the specified homogeneous open-chain infinite-size critical-tilt free-energy cotangent identity and N log N derivative with sharp subleading coefficient. Source sections discussing the chain stationary factorization, mean dissipation, and generic Gaussian large-deviation frameworks do not state that many-particle critical asymptotic. Both the spectral specialization and harmonic singular-sum estimate are required; searches do not establish uniqueness. Broad Gaussian or harmonic-network results remain an explicit residual risk.

value.rationale: The stationary law factorizes and ordinary entropy-production mean is extensive, yet the mean under rare-trajectory entropy tilt at the bulk edge is superextensive N log N. The sharp threshold, coefficient and next term quantify a meaningful many-body nonequilibrium fluctuation crossover. It is neither an arbitrary parameter slice nor a numerical recomputation; it resolves nonuniform finite-size scaling in a literature-motivated physical model. No general nonlinear or disordered claim is made.
